Detailed method

Thin ficelles. Currently 400 g flour, 70% hydration, 2% salt, and 0.8% yeast. That is 280 g water, 8 g salt, and 3.2 g yeast, 691.2 g of dough. Currently 4 sticks of 172.8 g each. Shorter in the oven than a baguette if you still want a soft middle. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 400 g flour, 280 g water, 8 g salt, and 3.2 g instant yeast until no dry flour remains, then knead about 6 minutes until smooth. At 70% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes and fold it once. With 0.8% yeast it should grow by about half.
  3. Shape Divide the 691.2 g into 4 pieces of 172.8 g each. Roll each piece into a thin stick about 40 cm long. Set them seam-side down on a floured cloth. The default 691.2 g uses a baking stone or tray about 40 cm long. If you change the amount, use a tray sized to fit, or bake in batches.
  4. Proof Cover the sticks for 25 to 40 minutes, until slightly puffy.
  5. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with a stone or tray for 30 minutes. Score one line along the top. Bake 12 to 16 minutes with steam, until the crust is golden. Take them out sooner if you still want a soft middle. Cool on a rack.
